summary: Inspected the shm/memory lifetime machinery at frozen head eb40eee: src/main.rs:557/6156-6196 (SLOT_RING=2 pinned ring, pool rebuilt only when slot count/byte size drifts, round-robin slot_rr so both slots reach final page footprint early, canvas()==None back-pressure, buffer/pool dropped before pool recreation so no double slabs), finish_unlock (src/main.rs:5547-5562, unconditional teardown of the lock-sized 2x24MB ring, lock_wallpaper, scale_scratch, morph scratches + malloc_trim, correctly NOT conditioned on a stage configure arriving), free_morph_scratches with capacity==0 no-op guard and iter125 collapse-settle freeing, M_MMAP_THRESHOLD/M_TRIM_THRESHOLD pinning at main() (src/main.rs:7526-7535), 60s idle malloc_trim, lazy ~19MB icon-font OnceLock with documented tradeoff, and the bounded 512-entry glyph cache with font-identity keying (src/lock_timer.rs:235-251). Read src/lockscreen.rs MAT_CACHE (972-1066): built once per lock, keyed on size/radius/wallpaper sig, held under the guard, released only by drop_lock_materials on a no-wallpaper lock frame — which main.rs never calls. Read /tmp/r3-verified-stress.log: load_leak compares like states (collapsed baseline 39 MB -> collapsed tail +0.0, peak +1.3 vs warmup 71, bound 8) — correct peak-vs-leak and reserved/RSS/Pss discipline; the log does not state whether that group exercises live lock cycling, so the 39MB collapsed baseline may already fold in the ~9MB lock-material retention below. No live lock cycles, captures, or captures-adjacent probes were run, per the brief. Verdict: ring-two discipline, teardown completeness and cache boundedness are source-verified and consistent with the like-state Pss evidence; one bounded-retention gap keeps it from a clean 10, nothing rises to blocker/major.

findings.title: ~9MB lock material cache (MAT_CACHE) survives unlock, contradicting its own release contract
findings.detail: with_lock_materials builds reg+blur (two w*h*3 buffers, ~9MB at 1504x1003) once per lock; drop_lock_materials() is only invoked from draw_lockscreen's no-wallpaper arm (src/lockscreen.rs:1301) and the doc comment at src/lockscreen.rs:1055-1058 explicitly expects main.rs to call it when leaving Lockscreen — but grep shows no main.rs call site on the frozen head. finish_unlock (src/main.rs:5546-5562) frees lock_wallpaper, scale_scratch, morph scratches and the shm ring, yet MAT_CACHE stays populated for the process lifetime after every lock preview exit, because the next draws are stage draws that never re-enter draw_lockscreen. Counterexample to 'harmless': this codebase itself treated a smaller 5.9MB scratch retention as a root cause (iter124/125) and made finish_unlock free-morph-scratches for exactly this reason; a ~9MB idle hold on a low-RAM target is the same class. Fix: call lockscreen::drop_lock_materials() (plus malloc_trim, already adjacent) in finish_unlock before apply_state_instant. Bound: single fixed-size cache, re-keyed and rebuilt on next lock, so not a leak — but re-adds the very 'first lock leaves RAM high' symptom iter124 chased.

findings.title: eDP asleep mid-preview can strand the lock-sized ring (source-only hypothesis, untested)
findings.detail: configure() (src/main.rs:6542-6557) zeroes configured_size and calls draw_if_ready; if the output sleeps while the lock preview is open (the startup log shows this exact condition happens on this hardware: zero-dimension configure + layer_surface_closed), no further draw fires and nothing re-enters finish_unlock, so the 2x~24MB lock ring plus scale_scratch/morph state stay mapped until the next wake-driven draw rebuilds them at stage size. Bounded (fixed-size, rebuilt not grown) and self-healing on wake, but the teardown being event-driven rather than state-driven means an asleep-output lock preview holds ~50MB reserved shm with no compositor consuming it. Cannot verify without live lock cycles (prohibited); flagging as unverified candidate, not an observed failure. Cheap hardening: the layer_surface_closed path could reuse the finish_unlock teardown block.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Call lockscreen::drop_lock_materials() from finish_unlock so the lock preview's ~9MB material cache is released on exit like every other lock-owned allocation (one line + existing malloc_trim), and harden the output-closed/zero-size path to run the same teardown so an asleep eDP mid-preview cannot strand the lock-sized ring. Optionally re-run the load_leak Pss gate with lock cycles inside the group so the collapsed baseline demonstrably excludes lock preview transients rather than folding them in.
